nodes.name: sans-IO core
nodes.responsibility: Owns application setup, registries, decorators, configuration, and extension-facing behavior without handling a live request.

nodes.name: WSGI application
nodes.responsibility: Implements the Flask WSGI entry point and coordinates request dispatch, response finalization, errors, teardown, and development serving.

nodes.name: contexts
nodes.responsibility: Creates, pushes, matches, and tears down application and request contexts for isolated request-scoped state.

nodes.name: globals
nodes.responsibility: Exposes current_app, request, session, g, and context proxies backed by application and request ContextVars.

nodes.name: routing
nodes.responsibility: Builds the URL map and rules, stores endpoint view functions, and provides adapters for URL matching and building.

nodes.name: blueprints
nodes.responsibility: Records reusable application setup and defers routes, handlers, templates, and commands until registration on an application.

nodes.name: CLI
nodes.responsibility: Discovers Flask applications, exposes the flask command group, loads app context for commands, and starts the development server.

nodes.name: sessions
nodes.responsibility: Defines the session interface and default signed-cookie session implementation used to open and save request sessions.

nodes.name: templating
nodes.responsibility: Creates Flask’s template loaders and renders templates with Flask context values and render signals.

nodes.name: JSON
nodes.responsibility: Provides the application JSON provider that serializes and deserializes values and creates JSON responses.

nodes.name: signals
nodes.responsibility: Declares Flask’s Blinker-backed lifecycle, request, template, and flashing signals for observers.

nodes.name: testing
nodes.responsibility: Provides Flask-aware HTTP clients, environment builders, session transactions, and CLI runners for tests.

nodes.name: werkzeug
nodes.responsibility: Supplies WSGI, HTTP, routing, request/response, local proxy, serving, and test primitives used by Flask.

nodes.name: jinja
nodes.responsibility: Supplies the template environment, loaders, template objects, and rendering engine used by Flask.

nodes.name: click
nodes.responsibility: Supplies the command, option, context, runner, and invocation primitives used by Flask’s CLI.

edges.label: push / pop RequestContext
edges.description: Flask.wsgi_app creates a request context, pushes it around full_dispatch_request, and pops it in finally.

edges.label: Flask extends App
edges.description: Flask in app.py subclasses the sans-IO App and reuses its registries and setup behavior.

edges.label: json.response
edges.description: make_response converts dict and list view return values through self.json.response.

edges.label: save_session
edges.description: process_response calls the configured session interface to save the request session into the response.

edges.label: request lifecycle signals
edges.description: full_dispatch_request and finalize_request send request_started and request_finished, while teardown paths send teardown signals.

edges.label: test client / CLI runner
edges.description: test_client and test_cli_runner construct FlaskClient and FlaskCliRunner instances.

edges.label: url_map / endpoints
edges.description: App initializes the URL map and add_url_rule stores rules and endpoint view functions.

edges.label: register_blueprint
edges.description: App.register_blueprint records the blueprint and calls blueprint.register(self, options).

edges.label: Jinja environment setup
edges.description: The sans-IO app owns the jinja environment configuration and uses the Flask templating loader integration.

edges.label: Map / Rule / adapter
edges.description: Flask creates Werkzeug Map and Rule objects and binds a MapAdapter for matching and URL building.

edges.label: deferred add_url_rule
edges.description: BlueprintSetupState.add_url_rule forwards registered blueprint rules to app.add_url_rule.

edges.label: register CLI commands
edges.description: Blueprint registration adds blueprint CLI commands to the application CLI group.

edges.label: bind ContextVars
edges.description: AppContext and RequestContext push and reset the _cv_app and _cv_request variables exposed by globals.

edges.label: match request URL
edges.description: RequestContext.match_request calls its URL adapter’s match method and stores the rule and view arguments.

edges.label: open_session
edges.description: RequestContext.push asks the configured session interface to open a session after the request context is available.

edges.label: app context signals
edges.description: AppContext.push and pop send appcontext_pushed and appcontext_popped.

edges.label: LocalProxy
edges.description: The public context globals are Werkzeug LocalProxy instances.

edges.label: current context values
edges.description: Template rendering obtains current_app and request, and the default processor injects request-scoped values.

edges.label: before / after render
edges.description: _render sends before_render_template before template.render and template_rendered afterward.

edges.label: load and render template
edges.description: Flask selects templates from the Jinja environment and invokes template.render or template.generate.

edges.label: response_class
edges.description: JSONProvider.response constructs the application’s response_class around serialized JSON.

edges.label: load Flask app
edges.description: ScriptInfo.load_app locates or creates the Flask application for commands.

edges.label: app context for commands
edges.description: with_appcontext loads the app and pushes app.app_context before invoking a command.

edges.label: run_simple
edges.description: run_command passes the loaded application to Werkzeug’s development server.

edges.label: commands and options
edges.description: FlaskGroup, AppGroup, and command decorators are built on Click primitives.

edges.label: CallbackDict
edges.description: SecureCookieSession uses Werkzeug’s CallbackDict for mutation tracking.

edges.label: exercise app
edges.description: FlaskClient inherits Werkzeug Client and opens requests against the Flask application.

edges.label: test and preserve contexts
edges.description: The test client creates test request contexts and can preserve them across a with block.

edges.label: session_transaction
edges.description: FlaskClient opens and saves sessions through the application session interface for isolated test transactions.

edges.label: HTTP test primitives
edges.description: EnvironBuilder and FlaskClient extend Werkzeug test builders and clients.

edges.label: CLI test runner
edges.description: FlaskCliRunner extends Click’s CliRunner to invoke app commands with ScriptInfo.
